item.title: Popondetta Police HQ decommissioned for new K1.5M facility
item.description: After 45 years of service to the people, the Popondetta Police Headquarters was decommissioned today to pave way for the construction of a new headquarters at the provincial capital. The project is funded under the Special Police Assistance Program (SPAP) by the Marape-Rosso Government, aimed at securing safer communities in partnership with provincial authorities.
item.content:encoded:
After 45 years of service to the people, the Popondetta Police Headquarters was decommissioned today to pave way for the construction of a new headquarters at the provincial capital.

The project is funded under the Special Police Assistance Program (SPAP) by the Marape-Rosso Government, aimed at securing safer communities in partnership with provincial authorities.

Speaking at the decommissioning ceremony, Deputy Commissioner of Police - Chief of Administration, Dr Philip Mitna said the SPAP has helped upgrade most of Papua New Guinea’s provincial police headquarters, and Popondetta’s is part of the infrastructure rehabilitation program.

"SPAP program has helped upgrade most of the Papua New Guinea provincial police headquarters, and Popondetta police headquarters is part of the infrastructure rehabilitation funded program." Dr. Mitna said.

Savana Construction Limited has been paid in full with over K1 million, and will begin construction of the new police headquarters for the province immediately following the decommissioning.

Northern Governor Gary Juffa thanked the National Government and the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary for ensuring the project was captured under SPAP.

Governor Juffa said the Oro Provincial Government’s priority is to mitigate law and order in the province, and it will continue to support the provincial police command to achieve its outcomes.

As part of that support, Governor Juffa presented a K100,000 cheque to Provincial Police Commander, Chief Inspector Charles Winuwan, to enhance administration. The remaining balance of K150,000 will be made available at a later date.

The Biru Correctional Service Institute also received K100,000 from the Oro Provincial Government, with a remaining balance of K150,000 to be paid later.

Governor Juffa said his government will work closely with RPNGC Headquarters to support the process of building the proposed two-level police headquarters for the province.

item.content:encoded:
‎ ‎A team from the Australian National University (ANU) in Australia and University of Papua New Guinea (UPNG) is in Milne Bay Province to study the province's diverse and deep cultural history. ‎ ‎The focus of the research is on the movement of people in the past.

The team comprises two male professors and a female PhD Archeology student from ANU and a lecturer and an Archeology final year student from UPNG. ‎ ‎Led by professor Dr. Ben Shaw from the Archaeology School of Culture, History and Language at the Australian National University, the research is specifically based on how the people in Milne Bay moved and settled thousands of years back. ‎ ‎"We are looking at how long people have lived in different places around Papua New Guinea on the islands, the mainland and who they interacted with" he said. "we are looking at the remains that people left behind; the shells that people ate, fish bones and fire places used thousands of years ago" ‎ ‎Dr. Shaw emphasized that once the research is concluded, all information gathered will be returned back to PNG. ‎ ‎"Our number one priority is to make sure the stories come back to the schools, communities, the people of Milne Bay first and foremost because that is where the research is conducted.” Dr Shaw said. ‎ ‎Dr Shaw added that the pillars they work by is honesty, transparency and respect when they are among communities in rural areas. ‎ ‎Meanwhile, the Head of Department in Anthropology, Archeology and sociology at UPNG, senior lecturer Vincent Kewibu says it's important for Papua New Guineans to be involved in this research as it is our very own culture and history. ‎ ‎"This is Papua New Guineas history, and people are now realizing the importance of our history as it is our identity and heritage at the same time.” He said. ‎ ‎The research in Milne Bay is a four-year project which started last year. ‎ ‎The team is currently making their way to Kimuta Island in the Lousiade LLG of Samarai -Murua District.

item.title: Busu Secondary School receives aid from Australian Government
item.description: More than 1600 students will benefit from new learning materials donated by the Australian Government. Busu Secondary School was privileged with the new materials, which will help them improve their knowledge.
item.content:encoded:
More than 1600 students will benefit from new learning materials donated by the Australian Government.

Busu Secondary School was privileged with the new materials, which will help them improve their knowledge.

Principal Mr George Noble acknowledged the continued support by the Australian Consulate, Brenton Kanowsky, notably from his prior visitations to school and to the distribution of the new materials.

Noble said, " we appreciate your generous support to the school and we want this partnership to continue."

Noble added," as you know, we were robbed of our computers in the laboratory and security is still pur great concern. And so I am just making a follow up to a submission to assist with fencing."

Noble appreciated the donation, because the school was struggling, to recoup all that were lost during the time of the break and entry.

Australian Consulate Brenton Kanowsky being aware of the recent break and entry of the school, has been in touch with the school principal for a couple of months before delivering the materials.

Kanowsky said, " I am happy to make this presentation to the school. I believe, these materials will benefit all the students to aid your education and enable you to be in a better position to guide you in your careers in the future."

The materials are delivered to the school, courtesy of their government partner, Lighthouse international.

Kanowsky also made a commitment to purchase a new camera for the school, to replace the last that was stolen with the other computer items in the laboratory.

item.title: ‎MBPHA holds training for IITT system
item.description: ‎The Milne Bay Provincial Health Authority (MBPHA) is conducting a weeklong important training for emergency medicine teams from Alotau Provincial Hospital and nearby health facilities. ‎The training aims to enhance the knowledge of its emergency first responders in using the newly recommended triage system known as the Integrated Interagency Triage Tool (IITT).
item.content:encoded:
‎The Milne Bay Provincial Health Authority (MBPHA) is conducting a weeklong important training for emergency medicine teams from Alotau Provincial Hospital and nearby health facilities.

‎The training aims to enhance the knowledge of its emergency first responders in using the newly recommended triage system known as the Integrated Interagency Triage Tool (IITT).

‎Despite the integrated Interagency Triage Tool (IITT) system being introduced in the Alotau Provincial Hospital emergency department, its effectiveness is limited due to lack of formal training for its emergency first responders and also the challenges faced with infrastructures.

‎The emergency first responders are not only the medical team but it's securities, clerical staff and janitors as they also play a very important part in entry in emergencies.

‎The triage system is designed to help emergency medical teams to assess and sort patients according to the urgency of their sickness when they arrive at the hospital using the colors red, yellow and green; red as emergency, yellow as urgent and green as non-urgent.

‎This ensures sicker patients are prioritized and helps prevent deaths and complications.

‎At the opening of training on Monday this week, Alotau Provincial Hospital Specialist Medical Officer of the Emergency Department, Dr. William Mataio, said the training is important as it empowers the emergency team to improve their care for patients.

‎"Emergency care in our setting has the potential to save a lot of lives, a lot of preventative deaths whether it be from injuries or from acute illness.

‎"This training is to empower us to improve our care in terms of prioritizing patients as they come to the hospital and to receive the best care they can.” Dr. Mataio said.

‎The training will also be extended to rural and remote health facilities within the province once the Provincial Hospital is completed.

‎The IITT system is recommended by World Health Organization (WHO) for Low-to Middle-income countries and by PNG society for Emergency Medicine (PNGSEM).

‎The training is supported by Regional Emergency and Critical Care Systems Strengthening Initiative (RECSI) through Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT),Australia, Port Moresby General Hospital and MBPHA.

item.title: PNGFA strengthens Futsal refereeing through FIFA MA referees course
item.description: The Papua New Guinea Football Association successfully concluded a FIFA Member Association (MA) Futsal Referees Course, reinforcing its commitment to developing qualified match officials and raising the standard of futsal across the country. The course was conducted from August 3rd to 7th at the PNG Football Stadium in Port Moresby.
item.content:encoded:
The Papua New Guinea Football Association successfully concluded a FIFA Member Association (MA) Futsal Referees Course, reinforcing its commitment to developing qualified match officials and raising the standard of futsal across the country.

The course was conducted from August 3rd to 7th at the PNG Football Stadium in Port Moresby.

The course was facilitated by FIFA Referee Instructor Neil Poloso of Solomon Islands, with support from PNGFA Referee Development Officer Samol Minan.

A total of 20 participants completed the course, comprising 16 male and 4 female referees representing a range of Member Associations, including Port Moresby Soccer Association (PMSA), National Capital District Football Association (NCDFA), Manus Soccer Association, Kimbe Soccer Association and Koupa Soccer Association.

Throughout the course, participants were introduced to the latest FIFA Futsal Laws of the Game and modern refereeing methodologies using FIFA's updated teaching materials.

The course combined theoretical learning with practical sessions aimed at equipping referees with the knowledge and confidence to officiate futsal matches to international standards.

PNGFA General Secretary Ahmjad Tekwie acknowledged the instructor, facilitators and participants for their commitment to the program.

“Thank you to Neil, Samol and all the participants for your dedication throughout the course. We look forward to seeing you apply what you have learned as the futsal competition gets underway,” Tekwie said.

FIFA Referee Instructor Neil Poloso commended PNGFA for investing in referee education and highlighted the importance of developing the next generation of futsal officials.

“I would like to thank PNGFA for hosting this very important course. It is an investment in the next generation of futsal referees, and I wish all the participants every success as they implement what they have learned throughout the season,” Poloso said.

Speaking on behalf of the participants, Andrew Marampau expressed appreciation to the instructors and PNGFA for delivering the program.

“We thank the facilitators for sharing their knowledge and empowering us to perform our duties as futsal referees.

“This course has given us a better understanding of the Laws of the Game, and we are now challenged to return to our associations, create awareness and pass on what we have learned to help grow futsal in Papua New Guinea,” Marampau said.

The successful completion of the FIFA MA Futsal Referees Course marks another important step in PNGFA's ongoing efforts to strengthen referee development and support the continued growth of futsal throughout Papua New Guinea.

item.title: 20 homeowners of Old Compound in Mendi receive keys to new houses
item.description: On Tuesday, August 18, 2026—four years to the day after severe election-related violence devastated Mendi Town, Governor William Powi and the Southern Highlands Provincial Administration presented 20 homeowners from the Old Compound community with keys, land titles, and allotment documents for their new homes. Old Compound, home to public servants from various provinces, was among the communities
item.content:encoded:
On Tuesday, August 18, 2026—four years to the day after severe election-related violence devastated Mendi Town, Governor William Powi and the Southern Highlands Provincial Administration presented 20 homeowners from the Old Compound community with keys, land titles, and allotment documents for their new homes.

Old Compound, home to public servants from various provinces, was among the communities hardest hit by the 2022 National Election related violence that destroyed parts of Mendi Town, leaving dozens homeless. After the rebuilding process, the name is New Compound.

The presentation brings the total number of rebuilt residences delivered to 40, with an additional 20 currently under construction as part of ongoing relief efforts.

​Speaking on behalf of the displaced families, former Deputy Provincial Administrator Fiebik Simon Kilip expressed appreciation to Governor Powi while reflecting on the trauma of the 2022 tragedy.

Kilip said, the new houses restore safety, dignity, and hope to the community. He also extended a message of forgiveness to those responsible for the destruction and urged PNG Power to install a power transmitter and restore electricity so residents can fully settle back into their homes.

"We stood helplessly and watched the homes we built with love turn to ash. With nothing in our hands, we fled with our children into the bushes of Tubiri Village, running only to save our lives.

"When those houses burnt, we did not just lose shelter. We lost the walls that held our childhood memories. We lost kitchens where mothers cooked for their families, rooms where children took their first steps, and places that carried the history of our families and our town. Businesses were destroyed. The properties of innocent people were gone in a single night. We were left with grief, trauma, and uncertainty." He said.

Kilip said for four years the community carried the memory, properties of innocents were gone in a single night and they were left with grief and uncertainty.

"The handing over of these house keys is more than the return of shelter. It is the restoration of dignity, security, and a future for our children. It is the beginning of new memories in homes built on the strength of our past.” He said.

Kilip said on behalf of those who suffered loss, they chose to forgive those who destroyed their houses and properties.

"On behalf of all who suffered loss, we choose forgiveness. We forgive those who destroyed our houses and properties. We release the bitterness so that we can build peace for our children," he said.

item.title: SoE Minister Duma to unveil PNG’s Sovereign Cloud and AI Datacenter
item.description: The Government of Papua New Guinea will mark a significant milestone in the country’s digital transformation journey on Friday, 21 August 2026, with the official inauguration of Kumul Cloud Infinity — PNG’s Sovereign Cloud and AI Datacenter, at the Sheraton Hotel, Port Moresby. The landmark facility, developed by Datec PNG and Telikom PNG, represents a major step towards strengthening Papua New Gu
item.content:encoded:
The Government of Papua New Guinea will mark a significant milestone in the country’s digital transformation journey on Friday, 21 August 2026, with the official inauguration of Kumul Cloud Infinity — PNG’s Sovereign Cloud and AI Datacenter, at the Sheraton Hotel, Port Moresby.

The landmark facility, developed by Datec PNG and Telikom PNG, represents a major step towards strengthening Papua New Guinea’s digital sovereignty, data security and national AI capabilities.

This will enable organisations to securely host, process and manage critical data and digital workloads within the country.

CEO of Datec PNG, Preetam Talukdar, said the launch represents a defining moment for both Datec and Papua New Guinea.

“Kumul Cloud Infinity is not simply a technology project. It is about sovereignty in its truest digital sense — giving Papua New Guinea the ability to control, protect and build upon its own digital future.”Talukdar said.

He said the initiative reflects Datec PNG and Telikom PNG’s commitment to investing in infrastructure that will enable Papua New Guineans, businesses and institutions to participate more confidently in the global digital economy.

Minister for State Enterprises, William Duma will lead the inauguration and unveil the new Kumul Cloud Infinity facility.

This new chapter in PNG’s digital sovereignty is to ensure that Papua New Guinea has the infrastructure and capability to own, control and protect its digital future.

Kumul Cloud Infinity is designed to provide a trusted in-country environment for cloud computing, artificial intelligence, data hosting, enterprise applications and other advanced digital workloads.

The initiative also brings together the capabilities of Datec PNG, Telikom PNG and international technology partners, creating a platform designed to support PNG’s growing digital economy and the next generation of technology-led businesses and services.

item.title: Buimo inmates graduate from pre-release training
item.description: One hundred inmates at Buimo Correctional Institution in Morobe graduated from a pre-release training program, equipping them with practical skills, knowledge and confidence for life after release. The program of eight weeks is aimed to support inmates to improve their livelihood opportunities, and reduce the risk of reoffending.
item.content:encoded:
One hundred inmates at Buimo Correctional Institution in Morobe graduated from a pre-release training program, equipping them with practical skills, knowledge and confidence for life after release.

The program of eight weeks is aimed to support inmates to improve their livelihood opportunities, and reduce the risk of reoffending.

Delivered by the Papua New Guinea Correctional Service with local partner Necktop Training Centre, and supported by the Australian Government through the Australia- Papua New Guinea Law and Justice Partnership, the program covered financial literacy, spiritual development, practical life skills and vocational training.

Participants also gained hands-on skills in areas such as coconut oil processing, helping prepare them for income-generating opportunities following release.

Australian High Commission Minister-Counsellor, Elizabeth Le Bas, said, “Australia is proud to support Papua New Guinea-led efforts to strengthen rehabilitation through its long-standing partnership with the Papua New Guinea Correctional Services.”

“If people leave custody without the skills or support to rebuild their lives, the challenges that brought them there often remain.

“But when people leave better prepared for what comes next, everyone benefits. Families are stronger and communities are safer,” she said.

For graduate Sharon Kamu, the training marked the beginning of a new chapter. Released on the same day she completed the program; she said the training helped rebuild her confidence and equipped her with practical skills to manage her finances and prepare for the future.

“The training resurrected my dreams and reminded me there is always a second chance,” Ms Kamu said.

Buimo Correctional Institution Commander, Michael Wundia, congratulated the 100 graduates and acknowledged Australia’s support for the program.

He commended the training for giving participants practical skills to support themselves, their families and communities after release. “Use these skills well, be good citizens and make the most of this opportunity when you return to your communities,” Mr Wundia said.

The Australia PNG Law and Justice Partnership is a PNG law and justice sector-led initiative, with programs prioritised through the National Coordinating Mechanism and delivered in partnership with sector agencies.
